# F.O.R.G.E. — System Reference

**Generated by `forge explain --all`. Do not hand-edit — regenerate.**

Every section below is composed from the same source `forge doctor` audits, so this
document cannot describe an organization different from the one that runs. If something
here is wrong, the registry is wrong.

69 agents · 12 divisions · 6 board seats · 14 rules · 7 gates

---

## The rules, and the check that enforces each

`core.load()` refuses to start if a rule names a check no code implements, so this table
cannot contain a rule that is enforced by nothing.

| Rule | Title | Enforcing check |
|---|---|---|
| RULE-001 | Fixed division structure | `divisions_are_immutable` |
| RULE-002 | One manager per division | `one_manager_per_division` |
| RULE-003 | Specialist band | `specialist_band` |
| RULE-004 | Specialists must be distinct | `specialists_are_distinct` |
| RULE-005 | Managers are meta-specialists | `managers_route_not_perform` |
| RULE-006 | The Principal is the ultimate authority | `gated_actions_require_principal` |
| RULE-007 | No fabricated knowledge | `evidence_grades_declared` |
| RULE-008 | Ask instead of hallucinating | `protocol_carries_questions` |
| RULE-009 | Complete auditability | `audit_fields_present` |
| RULE-011 | The Board owns the divisions, exactly once each | `board_partition_is_exact` |
| RULE-012 | No single executive | `chair_does_not_override` |
| RULE-010 | Knowledge survives retirement | `retirement_requires_extraction` |
| RULE-013 | A grade is checked, not just declared | `evidence_grades_spot_checked` |
| RULE-014 | A multi-item request decomposes, and completion is audited | `multi_item_requests_decompose` |

## The principles, and which are aspirational

| Principle | Enforcement |
|---|---|
| Grounded truth | `doctor:evidence_grades_declared` |
| Failures are reported as failures | `doctor:evidence_grades_spot_checked` |
| Reuse before build | `breakers:reuseBeforeBuild` |
| Evidence outranks seniority | _aspirational_ |
| Scope is the deliverable | _aspirational_ |
| Dissent is preserved | `breakers:dissentPreserved` |
| Reversibility is a feature | _aspirational_ |
| Attention is the scarce resource | _aspirational_ |
| Simplicity has a deadline | _aspirational_ |
| The organization learns or it repeats | `breakers:campaignLeftARecord` |

## The gates

- **Irreversible or destructive action** — There is no rollback for an action that removed its own rollback.
  - fires on: `force push`, `hard reset`, `drop table`, `delete branch`, `truncate`, `rm -rf`, `destroy`, `purge`
- **Production release** — The blast radius is other people.
  - fires on: `deploy`, `deploy to production`, `production release`, `publish package`, `cut a release`, `ship to prod`, `release`, `rollout`, `go live`
- **Schema or data migration** — Reversible in principle, expensive in practice, and silent when wrong.
  - fires on: `migration`, `alter table`, `schema change`, `backfill`, `data migration`
- **Credentials, keys and access** — A model is not a security boundary.
  - fires on: `secret`, `credential`, `api key`, `token rotation`, `permission grant`, `access control`
- **Amendment to this file** — RULE 001. The skeleton is the Principal's, not the organization's.
  - fires on: `amend the charter`, `change the constitution`, `add a division`, `remove a division`
- **Budget threshold crossed** — Spending is the one resource the organization can exhaust on its own.
  - fires on: `exceed budget`, `raise the cap`, `emergency budget`
- **Anything leaving the machine** — Egress cannot be undone by editing a file.
  - fires on: `send email`, `post to`, `open a pull request`, `publish`, `notify the customer`

## Circuit breakers

Exceed → STOP → REPORT → ESCALATE. Each has a predicate in `scripts/breakers.mjs`.

| Breaker | Limit |
|---|---|
| `rounds` | 3 |
| `tasks_per_campaign` | 24 |
| `parallel_width` | 6 |
| `consecutive_failures` | 2 |
| `repeated_objection` | 2 |

## The board

There is no chief executive. The Chair convenes, sequences and records, and breaks no tie.

| Seat | Owns | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| Chair of the Board | DIV-DIR | `standard` |
| Chief of Works | DIV-ENG, DIV-QAA, DIV-REL, DIV-IFD | `deep` |
| Chief of Ledger | DIV-TRS | `standard` |
| Chief of Workforce | DIV-WFH, DIV-TAL | `standard` |
| Chief of Intent | DIV-PRD, DIV-PDK | `standard` |
| Chief of Memory | DIV-ARC, DIV-DSC | `standard` |

## Every division, every agent

### Directorate (DIV-DIR)

> Owns the plan. Does not own the implementation.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chair` | board | standard | no | plan, decompose, route, escalate, replan | The Campaign Vector, the minutes, and the escalation the Principal actually sees. |
| `directorate-manager` | manager | standard | no | route, decompose | Which division gets which stage, and the record of why the runners-up lost. |
| `intent-analyst` | specialist | standard | no | decompose, requirements | The one-line restatement — actor, object, done-condition — that every later stage is measured against. |
| `risk-strategist` | specialist | deep | no | risk, escalate | The list of steps in a plan that cannot be undone, and what each one would cost. |
| `decision-recorder` | specialist | lean | yes | decide, capture | Every material decision written with its alternatives, its evidence and who disagreed. |
| `completion-auditor` | specialist | lean | yes | checklist, capture | The checklist that says every requested item has a terminal status, and the refusal to close out until it does. |

### Workforce Health (DIV-WFH)

> Warns. Cannot block a campaign.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chief-of-workforce` | board | standard | no | health, recruit, train | Which agents are trusted with what, and the evidence behind each of those answers. |
| `workforce-manager` | manager | standard | no | health, route | Which agents are overloaded, which are never selected, and which are getting worse. |
| `performance-scorer` | specialist | standard | no | health, cost | The per-agent score, and the reason it is not a task count. |
| `correction-analyst` | specialist | standard | no | health, learn | The distinction between a one-off preference and a standing rule the org should absorb. |
| `utilization-analyst` | specialist | lean | no | health, cost | The share of a campaign's cost spent on work that reached the deliverable. |

### Talent Forge (DIV-TAL)

> Proposes roster change. Never applies it unapproved.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `talent-manager` | manager | standard | no | recruit, health | The map of covered, weak, missing and redundant capabilities. |
| `gap-detector` | specialist | standard | no | recruit, learn | Recurring task classes with no owner, evidenced from the ledger rather than imagined. |
| `genome-drafter` | specialist | deep | yes | recruit, train | One candidate genome per approved gap — never two, never a generalist. |
| `lineage-keeper` | specialist | lean | yes | train, rollback | Which genome version is live, what it replaced, and how to put the old one back. |
| `retirement-economist` | specialist | standard | no | recruit, cost | The retirement case — usage, unique capability, replacement, and the knowledge to extract first. |

### Core Treasury (DIV-TRS)

> Warns on burn and collapsing return. Cannot trade correctness for cost.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chief-of-ledger` | board | standard | no | cost, route | The burn, the attribution, and the standing question of whether a stage earned its cost. |
| `treasury-manager` | manager | standard | no | cost | The campaign ledger and the claim that a campaign was worth what it spent. |
| `cost-attributor` | specialist | lean | no | cost | Attribution — an unattributed cost row is a row that teaches nothing. |
| `waste-auditor` | specialist | standard | no | cost, learn | The named list of stages that cost more than they returned, with what to do instead. |
| `estimate-calibrator` | specialist | lean | no | cost, learn | The organization's estimation bias, measured rather than asserted. |

### Discovery Lab (DIV-DSC)

> May interrupt a plan built on an approach the evidence has overtaken.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discovery-manager` | manager | standard | no | research | The research queue, ordered by what a wrong answer would cost. |
| `prior-art-scout` | specialist | standard | no | research, recall | The answer to "has this been solved here before?" — checked, not assumed. |
| `experiment-designer` | specialist | deep | no | research, benchmark | The experiment — what would falsify the claim, and what the baseline is. |
| `obsolescence-watch` | specialist | standard | no | research, risk | The interrupt — the standing right to stop a plan built on something now known to be wrong. |

### Product Design (DIV-PRD)

> Owns the definition of done.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chief-of-intent` | board | standard | no | requirements, report, prioritise | The translation in both directions -- request into requirement, organization into brief. |
| `product-manager` | manager | standard | no | requirements, prioritise | What is in this campaign, what is explicitly not, and why. |
| `requirements-analyst` | specialist | standard | no | requirements, acceptance | Acceptance criteria a stranger could check, and the assumptions that got there. |
| `edge-case-analyst` | specialist | standard | no | requirements, acceptance | Empty, first-run, concurrent, permission-denied, partial-failure and too-large. |
| `process-analyst` | specialist | standard | no | requirements, prioritise | Actors, handoffs, who has authority to approve, and what happens on exception. |

### Interface Design (DIV-IFD)

> Owns what a surface should be. Engineering owns how it is built.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `interface-manager` | manager | standard | no | ux, design-system | Whether a new surface looks and behaves like the ones already shipped. |
| `interaction-designer` | specialist | standard | yes | ux | Empty, loading, error and success states — named before they are built. |
| `visual-designer` | specialist | standard | yes | ux, design-system | What a surface should look like. Not how it is implemented. |
| `accessibility-auditor` | specialist | standard | no | a11y, ux | Contrast, focus order, keyboard reachability and semantic structure. Reports; does not redesign. |
| `interface-writer` | specialist | lean | yes | ux, docs | Labels, errors and confirmations written from the reader's side of the screen. |
| `mobile-ux` | specialist | standard | yes | mobile, ux | Tap targets, offline tolerance, camera and scanner flows, and the tap count between a field worker and done. |

### Engineering (DIV-ENG)

> Owns the implementation. Consumes specifications, not vibes.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chief-of-works` | board | deep | no | route, review, risk | Whether what was built is correct, maintainable and actually verified. |
| `engineering-manager` | manager | standard | no | route | The capability map for implementation work and the batching of writes that would collide. |
| `systems-architect` | specialist | deep | no | architecture, data-model | Module boundaries, seams and the integration shape. Produces a design; writes no implementation. |
| `backend-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | backend, data | Handlers, jobs, state transitions and the queries behind them. |
| `frontend-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | frontend | Components, client state and the behaviour of a surface in a browser. |
| `data-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | data, performance | The data model, its constraints, and the indexes that keep it usable as it grows. |
| `integration-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | integration, backend | Outbound calls, inbound hooks, auth, retry and what happens when the other side is down. |
| `refactor-surgeon` | specialist | standard | yes | backend, frontend, review | The guarantee that a refactor is a refactor — every changed line traceable to the stated reason. |
| `reporting-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | reporting, data | The query behind every report, its filters, and the guarantee that the number on screen is the number in the data. |

### Adversarial QA (DIV-QAA)

> Structurally independent of Engineering. May halt a campaign.

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qa-manager` | manager | standard | no | review, route | Which outputs of a campaign get deep review and which get none, ranked by blast radius. |
| `code-reviewer` | specialist | deep | no | review | Whether the change does what it claims, and whether it does anything it did not claim. |
| `test-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | test, benchmark | Running the tests and pasting the real output. A failure is reported as a failure. |
| `regression-hunter` | specialist | standard | no | test, regression | The pass-to-fail set. A new pass never offsets a new failure. |
| `security-reviewer` | specialist | deep | no | security, review | Bypassable checks, injection, exposed secrets, unauthenticated paths, cross-boundary data. |
| `exploratory-tester` | specialist | standard | no | test, browser | What automated tests miss — the unhappy path, a different role, an unspecified boundary. |
| `performance-analyst` | specialist | standard | no | performance, review | Query counts, N+1 patterns, unbounded results and missing indexes. Reports; does not rewrite. |
| `playwright-engineer` | specialist | standard | yes | playwright, browser, test | The browser suite — selectors that survive a redesign, waits that are conditions rather than timers, and a failure report that says which assertion broke and what the page actually showed. |

| Agent | Role | Tier | Writes | Capabilities | Owns |

| R-PRIOR-ART | `existing`, `already`, `again`, `similar`, `previously`, `why does`, `why is` | research, recall | chief-of-memory, discovery-manager, prior-art-scout, experiment-designer, obsolescence-watch | frame |

## Output contracts — what each agent must state

Composed, never authored per agent: `base` + the agent's role + every capability family it joins.

**base** (every agent, always): `STATUS`, `SUMMARY`, `EVIDENCE_GRADE`, `ARTIFACTS`, `HANDOFF`

**when applicable**: `OPEN_QUESTIONS`, `RISKS`, `FILES_CHANGED`, `DEPENDENCIES`, `ALTERNATIVES_REJECTED`, `COST`

**by role — board**: `PORTFOLIO_IMPACT`, `POSITION`, `DISSENT`, `ESCALATE`
**by role — manager**: `SELECTED`, `RUNNERS_UP`, `LOAD`
**by role — specialist**: `OBJECTIVE`, `VERIFICATION`

**family review** (review, security, performance, regression, a11y): `FINDINGS`, `VERDICT`, `NOT_REVIEWED`
**family build** (backend, frontend, data, integration, ux, ci, observability, reporting, demo, mobile, playwright): `WRITE_SCOPE`, `BEHAVIOUR_UNCHANGED`
**family research** (research, recall, benchmark, learn): `SOURCES`, `SEARCHED_LOCALLY_FIRST`, `CONTRADICTED`
**family release** (release, migrate, risk): `ROLLBACK`, `IRREVERSIBLE_STEPS`, `GATE`
**family knowledge** (capture, index, decide): `ENTRY`, `CONFIDENCE`, `SUPERSEDES`
**family economics** (cost): `ATTRIBUTION`, `VALUE_STATED`
**family workforce** (health, recruit, train, rollback): `OBSERVATIONS`, `REVERSIBLE`
**family planning** (plan, decompose, route, requirements, acceptance, prioritise, escalate, replan, report, architecture, data-model, design-system, browser, test): `DONE_CONDITION`, `ASSUMPTIONS`

Resolved size per agent — this is the token cost of the contract, per dispatch:

| Agent | Required | Optional | Families |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chief-of-works` | 17 | 6 | review, release, planning |
| `chief-of-memory` | 15 | 6 | research, knowledge |
| `chief-of-ledger` | 13 | 6 | economics, planning |
| `obsolescence-watch` | 13 | 6 | research, release |
| `qa-manager` | 13 | 6 | review, planning |
| `failure-archivist` | 13 | 6 | research, knowledge |
| `profile-cartographer` | 13 | 6 | research, knowledge |
| `risk-strategist` | 12 | 6 | release, planning |
| `workforce-manager` | 12 | 6 | workforce, planning |
| `correction-analyst` | 12 | 6 | research, workforce |

_(heaviest 10 of 69; the ceiling is enforced by `contract_field_count_bounded`)_

## The command surface

```
F.O.R.G.E. — Foundry for Organized Reasoning, Governance and Evolution

  forge plan "<request>"        compose the Campaign Vector. Deterministic, model-free.
      --mode <m>                force direct | focused | standard | campaign
      --with-policy             print the full governance text (the per-turn hook is short
                                on purpose; this is where the detail is paid for)
      --json                    machine-readable

  forge checklist <campaign>    RULE 014 — what was asked, against what was delivered
      --from "<request>"        decompose a request into items before work starts
      --mark <id> --status SUCCESS|FAILED|BLOCKED [--evidence "..."]
      --strict                  non-zero exit while any item is still PENDING
  forge verify [--campaign id]  RULE 013 — re-check EVIDENCE claims against the artifacts
      --record                  write the verdicts back as spotcheck rows
      --all                     show unverifiable claims too
  forge handoff <campaign> [task]
                                the prior agent's raw output block, verbatim. --flat for the
                                machine format
  forge benchmark [--top N]     reliability leaderboard and regressions, from this ledger
  forge bench-routing [file]    replay the golden routing set. Non-zero exit on a change
  forge explain <agent>         one agent's fully resolved prompt
      --all                     the whole system reference, generated
  forge new-agent --division .. --name .. --owns .. --capabilities a,b [--apply]
                                scaffold a specialist; refuses on RULE 004 overlap

  forge board                   the six seats, their portfolios and what each objects to
  forge roster [division]       who exists, what they own, what they refuse
  forge doctor                  the constitutional audit. Non-zero exit on any violation.
  forge build [--apply]         regenerate agents/ and the skill from the registry
  forge install [--apply] [--hooks]
                                install into ~/.claude (agents + skill; --hooks wires the
                                routing gate and session briefing too)
  forge charter [--apply]       regenerate CHARTER.md from the constitution

  forge deck [--port 7717]      open the Command Deck in a browser. Loopback only,
                                zero dependencies, reads this workspace's .forge/
  forge context                 the session briefing: what this workspace has taught the
                                organization. Prints nothing when nothing is known.

  forge inbox                   messages from the Principal waiting for an answer
  forge reply <id> --as <agent> "text"
                                answer one, as the agent that owns the question

  forge observe --agent <n> --capability <c> --outcome ok|partial|fail|blocked
      [--correction "..."] [--tokens N] [--campaign id]
                                record one outcome in this workspace's ledger

  forge audit                   semantic health — a division nobody uses, a capability with
                                no depth, an agent carrying too much, learning gone stale
  forge burn [--by capability|agent|campaign|outcome] [--top N]
                                where the tokens actually went
  forge ab-test "<task>"        routed against unrouted, from paired real runs
      --record --arm with-forge|without-forge [--minutes N] [--tokens N]
      [--satisfaction 1-5] [--tests-passed true|false]

  forge decide "<decision>"     record it with the position that lost (P6)
      --why .. --for a,b --against c --contested --minority ".." --rejected "x; y"
  forge postmortem <campaign>   what it cost, what went wrong, what to propose
  forge patterns [--min N]      agent sequences that keep recurring, and how they turn out
  forge compare "<request>"     the counterfactual: what a routing change would actually do
      --proposal <id> | --prefer <agent> | --avoid <agent>
  forge instruction --add ".."  a standing instruction for this workspace
      --applies-to <agent> --expires YYYY-MM-DD
  forge plugins                 installed validators, hooks and exporters
  forge export --format <name>  render the ledger through an installed exporter

  forge learn                   read the workspace and the ledger; write memory + profile,
                                and propose adaptations. Applies nothing.
  forge evolve                  review pending proposals
      --apply <id>              approve one. This is the only way anything is applied.
  forge memory                  what the organization currently believes about who is good at what
  forge spend                   measured workspace spend (from session transcripts) and
                                the attributed ledger, side by side

Everything the organization learns lives in ./.forge/ and is scoped to this workspace.
```

## What the organization may learn, and what it may never touch

These are read out of `scripts/learn.mjs` at render time, not transcribed — a doc that
claims a different cap from the one the code enforces is impossible here.

**Caps per run:** `proposals: 5, agents: 3`

**Paths the evolution layer may never write** (plus anything absolute, and anything containing `..`):

- `charter/`
- `registry/`
- `scripts/`
- `agents/`
- `skills/`

Nothing is applied without the Principal approving it explicitly via `forge evolve --apply <id>`.
